raw_response:
I've been farming these fields for 35 years, ever since I was 15. Never went to school — can't read the fertilizer bags, so I just remember the colors and what the shopkeeper tells me. My husband and my son both work at a factory in the county town, so most days it's just me and my daughter-in-law at home. We have 16.9 mu, which is enough to keep us busy but not enough to hire machines for everything.

This year, the cotton goes on 10 mu like always. That's our cash crop. Lao Wang next door bought some new hybrid seeds last year and did well, so I'll do the same — I bought two big bags of cotton seed from the shop. For fertilizer, I put down one big bag of that compound stuff per mu when I plant in April, and then another half bag of white urea when the cotton starts flowering in July. Last year I did about the same and got roughly 1200 jin of seed cotton per mu. I don't know exactly how many kilograms that is, but the buyer pays by the jin so that's what I count. Cotton always needs spraying for bugs — I buy whatever insecticide the shop has, usually three or four times over the summer, plus some herbicide for the weeds. I'll water three times from the well: once after planting if the rain doesn't come, once when it's hot in July, and once in August when the bolls are fat. The electricity for the pump is expensive now, so I watch that closely. Picking is the hard part — me and my daughter-in-law can't pick 10 mu alone, so I hire women from the village for a few weeks in September and October. I pay them by the jin picked.

For wheat, I planted 6.9 mu last fall. It's already in the ground. Right now I need to spread some urea on it — about one small bag for every three mu — and water it at green-up. Then another watering when the heads are forming, and maybe one more before it turns yellow. We should cut it around early June. I don't hire anyone for wheat; we can manage the harvest ourselves, and the thresher man comes to the village with his machine.

Maize goes in right after the wheat comes off — no time to waste, maybe just one pass with the small tractor to chop the stubble, then plant by hand or with the machine. I'll put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and then topdress with urea when the maize is knee-high in July. Water it twice in the summer if it stays dry. We grow that maize partly for our own chickens and pigs, and sell whatever we don't eat.

I also plant mungbean between the cotton rows on about 3 mu. It doesn't need much — just some seed and maybe one watering in July. We harvest it in August before cotton picking starts. It's extra food and a little cash at the market.

Money is always tight. My husband sends some back from town, but I still have to watch every yuan. I'm spending about 6,500 yuan on the cotton alone, and another few thousand on the wheat and maize. Total will be around 9,800 yuan for the year. I always worry that the bugs might be bad or the well water might cost too much, but you do what you know. I'd rather put down a little extra fertilizer than risk a bad year — losing money on a bad crop hurts more than saving a few yuan on inputs.
